classification_scale.D: Small generic plugin API extension required

entries.rationale: The bridge has no OpenCPN-private dependency and linked successfully into a conventional plugin.
entries.qualification: An in-process engine shares the native plugin's crash boundary.

entries.rationale: A plugin-private bridge loaded a wasm32-wasip2 component from an explicit path.
entries.qualification: Package paths and identity must be validated before loading.

entries.rationale: Initialize, enable, action, disable and destroy completed inside stock OpenCPN.
entries.qualification: Long callbacks must be marshalled off the UI thread.

entries.rationale: The host can enumerate its own writable package root without core state.
entries.qualification: It must not scan or modify managed native-plugin directories.

entries.rationale: Verified staging, atomic replacement and rollback are plugin-owned, but installation UI and writable-root policy move into the host.
entries.qualification: Child install is invisible to OpenCPN Plugin Manager.

entries.rationale: Checksums, Ed25519 signatures, archive bounds, path rules and target validation are core-independent.
entries.qualification: Development keys are not production trust roots.

entries.rationale: The host can update child packages atomically, but needs its own catalogue, consent, failure and rollback UX.
entries.qualification: This creates a second governed update channel.

entries.rationale: The host owns instances and can add/retract their contributions independently.
entries.qualification: OpenCPN still enables only the outer plugin.

entries.rationale: Capability checks are host-owned, but the current static permission set needs persistent consent, revision and revocation semantics.
entries.qualification: Native helpers remain a higher-risk permission class.

entries.rationale: A plugin can render native consent UI, but package updates and newly requested permissions need a redesigned state machine.
entries.qualification: OpenCPN's native Plugin Manager does not display child grants.

entries.rationale: A host-owned writable root can be namespaced by package and exposed only through value APIs.
entries.qualification: GetPluginDataDir is installer-owned and read-only, not the writable package store.

entries.rationale: Plugin-owned native dialogs can grant individual paths and copy values for guests.
entries.qualification: Directory-wide ambient access must not be inferred from one selection.

entries.rationale: A plugin can provide constrained HTTP and write only to package-private storage, but proxy, certificate, redirect and cancellation policy require redesign.
entries.qualification: Never grant raw sockets by default.

entries.rationale: Memory-only/session credentials and platform-specific keychains are possible, but the public API has no portable secure credential store.
entries.qualification: A generic OpenCPN credential broker would upgrade this to D-quality production support.

entries.rationale: A plugin can own bounded workers and publish progress snapshots without blocking the UI thread.
entries.qualification: All UI operations must return to the UI thread.

entries.rationale: Cooperative guest cancellation plus host worker cancellation and bounded joins were exercised.
entries.qualification: Blocking third-party native calls need separate process deadlines.

entries.rationale: The bridge configures memory, instance, fuel and epoch ceilings without core help.
entries.qualification: Host-process OOM or Rust panic remains outside the Wasm limit boundary.

entries.rationale: A managed plugin may ship target helpers and launch them, but paths, protocols and target payloads must be repackaged for the host.
entries.qualification: Native helpers are not component-portable.

entries.rationale: Linux namespaces/rlimits, Windows Job Objects and macOS sandbox profiles offer useful target-specific containment.
entries.qualification: The guarantees differ across desktop, Flatpak and Android; plugin ownership adds no privilege.

entries.rationale: Plugin-owned wx dialogs and menus can render bounded declarative models, but current UI is coupled to large core-facing host classes.
entries.qualification: Schema versioning, accessibility and translations need explicit package metadata.

entries.rationale: The host registered manager, iGRIB and iWeatherRouting as distinct public SVG tools.
entries.qualification: They remain owned by the outer plugin.

entries.service: Multiple toolbar icons from one native host plugin
entries.rationale: Multiplicity and independent callback IDs are supported and used in production.
entries.qualification: GetToolbarToolCount is not a child-identity contract.

entries.rationale: Late insertion works publicly when followed by SetToolbarToolViz to force a rebuild.
entries.qualification: Insertion itself does not request rebuild; the workaround is beta-fragile.

entries.rationale: The host can persist package_id plus action_id and map it to transient native IDs.
entries.qualification: OpenCPN has no stable child action key.

entries.rationale: The host can persist checked/hidden preferences by logical key.
entries.qualification: Stock toolbar customisation excludes plugin tools and cannot preserve placement by child identity.

entries.rationale: SVG normal/rollover/toggled variants use core scaling; validated raster fallback is possible.
entries.qualification: No explicit disabled SVG or complete cross-target visual validation exists.

entries.rationale: Dynamic removal, reload and final cleanup completed with an empty registry.
entries.qualification: The host must stop dispatch before component destruction.

entries.rationale: The public API supports owned context items with visibility and enabled state.
entries.qualification: Application menu-bar insertion is not a general public child-action surface.

entries.rationale: The host can present a package manager and per-package preferences in its own dialog.
entries.qualification: Children cannot receive separate OpenCPN Plugin Manager preference entries.

entries.rationale: Complex modeless plugin-owned windows are established production practice.
entries.qualification: All lifetime and theme changes remain the host's responsibility.

evidence: P3 software and GL stock-host probes
entries.rationale: The host rendered an immutable five-point guest scene through both public callbacks.
entries.qualification: Scene decoding and publication must be bounded and lock-light.

entries.rationale: The host can receive chart mouse/keyboard/cursor events and test them against retained geometry.
entries.qualification: The package sees host-defined semantic events, never wx event objects.

entries.rationale: Position, heading, speed and cursor callbacks are supported public plugin capabilities.
entries.qualification: Snapshots need timestamps and stale-state semantics.

entries.rationale: Public value APIs enumerate and retrieve routes without private pointers.
entries.qualification: Copy into bounded runtime-owned values before worker use.

entries.rationale: Public APIs enumerate, retrieve, add, update and delete waypoints.
entries.qualification: Mutations require explicit user intent and stale-object checks.

entries.rationale: Production plugins create routes using the supported API.
entries.qualification: Host confirmation, rollback and GUID ownership rules are required.

entries.rationale: Plugins can inspect chart metadata and provide coarse coastline crossing, but no supported, batched authoritative coverage query matches the WIT name.
entries.qualification: Rename the current service or add a generic chart-query API.

entries.rationale: A display-only coastline approximation is public; authoritative point/depth/hazard semantics require a narrow generic public service.
entries.qualification: Never market the approximation as navigation safety.

entries.rationale: The host can supervise providers, caches and helpers internally, but the monolithic current host needs decomposition.
entries.qualification: Large frames should use immutable bounded snapshots or broker transport.

entries.rationale: Typed internal service routing is independent of OpenCPN core.
entries.qualification: Provider versions and permission intersections must be enforced.

entries.rationale: The host can broker typed values and semantic versions, but discovery, failure and backpressure contracts need formalisation.
entries.qualification: No direct guest-to-guest pointers or calls.

entries.rationale: Synchronous broadcast JSON supports useful interoperability.
entries.qualification: It provides no authentication, addressed ownership, binary lifetime safety or capability discovery.

entries.rationale: The host can load catalogues and resolve child translation keys, but OpenCPN recognises only the host's native identity.
entries.qualification: Package locale fallback and catalogue trust need design.

entries.rationale: The host can prefix and rate-limit child logs and include package/action identity.
entries.qualification: Untrusted text needs redaction and size limits.

entries.rationale: The host can expose package health, failures, versions, jobs and helper status in its manager.
entries.qualification: OpenCPN's crash UI cannot inherently attribute a native host crash to one child.

entries.rationale: Guest traps return errors and the host can retract contributions.
entries.qualification: Fuel, epoch and memory ceilings must remain mandatory.

entries.rationale: An external runtime broker can isolate engine/guest aborts, but a purely in-process plugin cannot protect OpenCPN from its own native faults.
entries.qualification: Use hybrid process isolation before accepting third-party production packages.

evidence: repository search: no production telemetry contract
entries.rationale: Telemetry is not required for the useful proof and adds consent/governance burden.
entries.qualification: Local opt-in diagnostics are sufficient initially.

entries.rationale: The outer runtime is a normal managed plugin and children can look first-class on the toolbar and in the runtime manager.
entries.qualification: Children cannot be separate native Plugin Manager entries.

entries.rationale: The native host can use the normal catalogue; bundled runtime/helpers need target packages and CI.
entries.qualification: Child cataloguing is a second ecosystem unless governance is accepted.

entries.rationale: Cryptographic verification works, but production roots, key rotation, provenance and signer policy are unresolved governance work.
entries.qualification: Native helper signatures and platform code signing are additional layers.

entries.rationale: The host can consume a signed revocation list, but secure distribution, emergency refresh and catalogue policy need a generic trusted update/governance decision.
entries.qualification: Fail closed for explicitly revoked signer/package/version tuples.

entries.rationale: Managed packages may carry libraries/helpers, but symbol isolation, DLL lookup, codesigning and vulnerability cadence require per-target design.
entries.qualification: Do not depend on another plugin's Wasmtime copy.

entries.rationale: Toolbar, Wasmtime, software/GL overlays, jobs, navigation enumeration and helper cleanup were exercised locally.
entries.qualification: Distribution tarball/Flatpak remain separate gates.

entries.rationale: The engine and managed plugin patterns support aarch64, but the host and helpers require target CI/runtime evidence.
entries.qualification: Do not claim support before target conformance.

entries.rationale: Managed plugins and private helpers are supported inside the sandbox, but downloads, spawning, portals and bwrap nesting need actual SDK tests.
entries.qualification: A child cannot escape or enlarge the OpenCPN Flatpak permissions.

entries.rationale: No API blocker was found, but DLL dependencies, Job Objects, MSVC ABI and signing need target builds.
entries.qualification: Current study did not execute Windows.

entries.service: macOS Intel and Apple Silicon host
entries.rationale: No architectural API blocker was found, but hardened runtime/JIT, notarisation, helper signing and universal/dual artifacts require tests.
entries.qualification: Current study did not execute macOS.

evidence: portable runtime CMake currently rejects Android
Wasmtime platform support: no 32-bit compiler backend
entries.rationale: The useful desktop preview should defer Android; JIT/executable-memory, 32-bit ABI, plugin packaging and helper process assumptions are unresolved.
entries.qualification: Android arm64 might be a later dedicated interpreter/AOT investigation, not a claimed target.

entries.rationale: Separate installation, catalogue, enablement, permissions and crash attribution in OpenCPN's own manager require core recognition of child packages.
entries.qualification: This is not required for a useful toolbar-first beta.

entries.service: Depth, hazard and chart object queries
entries.rationale: Private chart internals are unacceptable; a bounded, immutable, generic batch query is the clean production route if the workload truly needs it.
entries.qualification: Defer from the first vertical slice.
